name: gemm
notes:
One program for every (m, k, n): the shape reaches it through CRs and four loops -- the
token loop (dynamic, m rows of y), the output-channel tile loop (one row of R_ACC is 128 channels),
the k chunk loop (a's 128-lane rows) and the input loop inside a chunk -- so a whole layer
(4096 tokens x 1024 channels x 2880 inputs) is one launch, not one launch per tile, and the host
only launches. a is token-major (token i's k elements in rows i*chunks+c); w is *input-major*, row
t*wtiles+tt holding input channel t's weights for the tile of channels tt*128..tt*128+127 (column n
pads the last tile, row k the input loop's last prefetch); b is the n biases in its own region, one
row per tile; y is one row per token and tile. The inner loop is the outer product: one word does
MULT.RC.VE of the tile's 128 weights (R_CYCLIC slot 0) against the scalar a[i,t] (R0[t mod 128]) and
ACC.ADD into the tile's 128 FP32 accumulators, so each word is 128 useful MACs and the whole of k is
contracted inside the kernel -- no partial ever leaves XMEM and no host step joins anything. The word
also prefetches the next input's w row (MULT reads R_CYCLIC at cycle start) and advances the two
counters kept one ahead, so the multiply, the accumulate, the load and the branch all ride in one
word; the tile's b row sits in R1 for the whole pass, which lets the store word do the bias add
(MULT.VE x CR1 + ACC.ADD) and ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE identity in the same word. A short last chunk stops
at k - 128*(chunks-1) inputs and lanes past k multiply the packer's zeros, so nothing is wasted on
the k tail; the store's DS names 128 lanes for a full tile and n - 128*(ytiles-1) for the last, so a
row's scale never sees a lane past n. Every instruction is a hardware one, the golden is a float64
matmul of the values XMEM holds, and the cases pass with the store's quantization as the only
rounding (max |err| inside one step of the row grid). Domain: m 1..4096, k 1..2944, n 1..1024,
